title: A Colony for the Horizon
premise: Kestrel Blackwood investigates impossible accidents across the silent colonies of the Meridian Line, hiding a past she barely remembers. When the name 'Kestrel Blackwood' appears on the manifest of the Halcyon—a colony ship that never launched—she discovers she is one of two women carrying that identity: the original, frozen aboard the never-flown ship, and the copy who walked away. As factions fight over which half of humanity's cryosleepers will wake, Kestrel must expose the sabotage that stranded the Halcyon, confront the man who split her identity to save her, and choose between erasing herself or letting the original live. In the end, both women share the waking world—one as witness, one as judge—and the first trial held outside any law begins.
about_author: Quentin Quintana is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years routing cargo between orbital stations before turning to fiction. He writes at sea, claiming that stories, like ships, only hold together under pressure.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She closes an investigation into a station fire that shouldn't have been survivable, revealing her talent for reading accidents like confessions. A coded message arrives referencing a ship that never flew. Beat: restless competence masking loneliness; the hook lands in the final line.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She pulls the Halcyon's sealed records and finds her own name listed among two thousand cryosleepers—with her exact biometric signature. The archivist who helps her disappears within hours. Beat: dread and vertigo as identity itself becomes the mystery.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ilsa Vane, the Halcyon's original Kestrel, dreaming inside cryosleep of a life she never lived. Her fragments mirror Kestrel's own missing memories. Beat: eerie intimacy; the reader learns the copy and the original are bleeding into each other.

chapters.title: The Man Who Split Her
chapters.summary: Kestrel tracks down Dr. Aurel Senn, the neuroengineer who copied dying passengers' minds into new bodies after the Halcyon's launch was sabotaged. He confesses he made dozens of them—including her. Beat: betrayal curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Justice Without a Court
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Concord, the colonies' collapsed legal authority, moves to seize the Halcyon's sleepers as salvage. Kestrel realizes the 'impossible accidents' she investigated were targeted killings of witnesses to the sabotage. Beat: righteous anger; stakes widen from personal to civilizational.

chapters.title: Two Thousand Sleeping Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, surfacing briefly during a power fluctuation. She wakes enough to record a message naming the saboteur—an official now leading the Concord's salvage claim. Beat: hope and terror entwined; the dead ship becomes a courtroom.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She races the Concord fleet to the Halcyon's drifting hull, smuggling Senn and the evidence aboard through a debris field. An old ally sells her out. Beat: rising action, sacrifice, and the cost of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Boarded by the Concord, Kestrel must choose: wake the sleepers illegally and trigger war, or let them sleep and lose the only proof. She initiates a partial revival—Ilsa among them—as boarding parties breach the hull. Beat: decisive courage under impossible pressure.

chapters.title: The Trial of Kestrel Blackwood
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Awake for the first time, Ilsa faces her copy. Together they testify against the saboteur before an improvised jury of the newly woken—justice outside any law. The Concord fractures when the truth broadcasts system-wide. Beat: catharsis; two identities refusing to erase each other.

chapters.title: A Colony for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POVs. The Halcyon's survivors found a settlement governed by their own improvised law, with Kestrel and Ilsa as its first dual magistrates. Senn accepts exile; memory, not blood, defines who they are. Final image: the two women watching the same horizon from different windows. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
